policy: Real-time telemetry, watershed chemistry, macroinvertebrate health, and weather-station streams are environmental-monitoring context maintained by Seminole County and partners. They describe watersheds, source water, and infrastructure - not the treated water at a household faucet.

sources.name: Seminole County Water Atlas (County + USF)
sources.authority: Seminole County / University of South Florida
sources.notes: Most vital local source: real-time water resource mapping, water chemistry query, live water-quality indicators.
sources.biological_health_note: Stream Condition Index (SCI) is the macroinvertebrate-based biological health metric; Lake Vegetation Index (LVI) covers lake flora.
sources.data_caveat: Near-real-time data have not passed the quality-control procedures applied to the Atlas's other datasets.

sources.name: Seminole County Surface Water Quality Program
sources.records: Hydrological metrics, biological macroinvertebrate health, and 15 automated meteorological and telemetry weather stations across major watersheds

sources.name: Seminole County GIS Data Library
sources.authority: Seminole County GIS / Public Works Engineering & Mapping
sources.assets: Pipeline assets, spatial imagery, capital engineering metrics, storm drainage features

disclaimer: Environmental and infrastructure monitoring context only; these streams are not household tap-water samples and not automatically a public water system compliance result.
